config.title: App Shell & Navigation

intro.title: App Shell & Navigation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application with a basic app shell and navigation. You'll learn how to structure your app with a main layout component that serves as the app's shell, containing a header and a navigation bar. The core concept is using Angular's Router to define routes and navigate between different views without reloading the page. You'll work with key Angular constructs like components, the RouterModule, and routerLink directives. By the end, you'll have a functional app that can switch between pages smoothly, giving you a foundation for building more complex Angular applications.
intro.usecase: App shells and navigation patterns are fundamental to creating professional web applications like e-commerce platforms, banking dashboards, and content management systems. In an e-commerce site, the app shell provides persistent elements like the header with logo, search bar, and shopping cart icon, while navigation controls allow users to move between product categories, deals, and account settings. Developers implement these patterns to ensure consistent user experience across all pages while managing state and loading performance. This approach is also crucial for admin panels where navigation between data tables, analytics, and user management must remain fluid and predictable.

objectives: Construct a new Angular application with routing enabled using the Angular CLI.
Apply the RouterModule to configure application routes in the AppModule.
Implement router-outlet directives to display routed components in the application shell.
Utilize routerLink directives in template elements to create navigation links between views.
Define route configurations with path and component properties to map URLs to components.
Execute navigation programmatically using the Router service's navigate method.
Handle route parameters to access dynamic data from URL segments.
Control navigation flow by applying route guards to protect specific routes.
Modify the application shell template to include persistent navigation elements.
Access route information and state using ActivatedRoute service in components.
Implement nested routes to create hierarchical navigation structures within the application.
Use Angular's built-in CSS classes to style active navigation links based on current route.

steps.title: Import Angular core modules
steps.instruction: Add import statements for Component and NgModule from @angular/core.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbols you want to import from the module path.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular core modules Component and NgModule are imported, making them available for use in your application.
successCriteria: The code includes a valid import statement that imports both Component and NgModule from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the core Angular modules. This gives you access to the Component decorator for creating components and the NgModule decorator for defining modules.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the import statement needs both Component and NgModule from '@angular/core'. Check the syntax and make sure both symbols are included.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both Component and NgModule from '@angular/core' using the correct import syntax.

steps.title: Import Angular router modules
steps.instruction: Add an import statement for RouterModule and Routes from the @angular/router package.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the module names in curly braces, then specify the package path.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing from @angular/router
import { RouterModule, Routes } from '@angular/router';
steps.expectedOutcome: The @angular/router package is imported, making RouterModule and Routes available for use in your Angular application.
successCriteria: The code includes a valid import statement that imports both RouterModule and Routes from '@angular/router'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported RouterModule and Routes. These are essential for setting up routing in Angular.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your import statement. Make sure you're importing both RouterModule and Routes from '@angular/router'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import RouterModule and Routes from '@angular/router' to enable routing.

steps.title: Create the AppComponent
steps.instruction: Create the main AppComponent class with the @Component decorator and an empty template.
steps.hint: Define a class named AppComponent and decorate it with @Component, providing an empty template string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class is defined with the @Component decorator and an empty template.
successCriteria: template property set to empty string
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the AppComponent with the @Component decorator and an empty template. This is the root component of your Angular application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have: 1) A class named AppComponent, 2) The @Component decorator applied to it, and 3) The template property set to an empty string (template: '').
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppComponent wasn't created correctly. You need to define a class named AppComponent with the @Component decorator that has an empty template.

steps.title: Define route configuration
steps.instruction: Define a constant named 'routes' of type 'Routes' (from @angular/router) and initialize it as an empty array.
steps.hint: Use the 'Routes' type you imported earlier. Create a constant with the 'const' keyword.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of defining a routes array
const routes: Routes = [];
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a 'routes' constant defined that can later hold your route definitions.
successCriteria: The code should include a constant named 'routes' typed as 'Routes' and initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the routes array. This empty array will serve as the foundation for your application's navigation structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a constant named 'routes' with the correct type 'Routes' and initialized it as an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The routes array isn't properly defined. You need to create a constant named 'routes' of type 'Routes' and set it to an empty array.

steps.title: Create AppModule
steps.instruction: Create the main application module by defining a class named AppModule with the @NgModule decorator.
steps.hint: Use the NgModule decorator imported earlier. The class should be exported.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppModule class is defined with the @NgModule decorator, ready to be configured in the next steps.
successCriteria: The code should include an exported class named AppModule decorated with @NgModule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the AppModule class with the @NgModule decorator. This is the root module that will bootstrap your Angular application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the @NgModule decorator applied to the class and the class is exported as AppModule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppModule class with @NgModule decorator is not correctly defined. Check that you've used the NgModule decorator and exported the class.

steps.title: Declare AppComponent in AppModule
steps.instruction: Inside the AppModule class, add AppComponent to the declarations array in the @NgModule decorator.
steps.hint: The declarations array should include AppComponent. Make sure to import AppComponent if it's not already imported.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent is properly declared in the AppModule, making it available for use in the application.
successCriteria: The AppModule's @NgModule decorator includes a declarations array containing AppComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully declared AppComponent in the AppModule. This is essential for Angular to recognize and use your root component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure AppComponent is included in the declarations array of the @NgModule decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppComponent needs to be declared in the AppModule. Check that you've added it to the declarations array in the @NgModule decorator.

steps.title: Import RouterModule in AppModule
steps.instruction: Add RouterModule.forRoot(routes) to the imports array in the @NgModule decorator of AppModule.
steps.hint: Inside the @NgModule decorator, add RouterModule.forRoot(routes) to the imports array. This configures the router with your defined routes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppModule will have routing configured, enabling navigation throughout the application.
successCriteria: RouterModule.forRoot(routes) is added to the imports array in the @NgModule decorator.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully configured routing in the AppModule. The router is now ready to handle navigation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure RouterModule.forRoot(routes) is inside the imports array of the @NgModule decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The routing configuration is missing. Add RouterModule.forRoot(routes) to the imports array in the @NgModule decorator.

steps.title: Add navigation shell to AppComponent template
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent's @Component decorator, add a template property with a header containing navigation links and a router-outlet element.
steps.hint: The template should be a multi-line string using backticks (`). Include a <header> with <nav> and <a> tags using routerLink directives, and add <router-outlet> below.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will have a template with a navigation header and router outlet for rendering routed components.
successCriteria: The AppComponent's @Component decorator includes a template property with: 1) A <header> containing <nav> with at least two <a> tags using routerLink, 2) A <router-outlet> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the app shell template with navigation links and router outlet.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your template includes both the navigation header with routerLink attributes and the router-outlet element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a template property to the @Component decorator with the required navigation structure and router-outlet.

steps.title: Create HomeComponent
steps.instruction: Create a new component named HomeComponent with the @Component decorator and a simple template that displays a heading.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define the component. Set the selector to 'app-home' and add a template property with an <h2> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A HomeComponent class is created with a basic template, ready to be used as a route component.
successCriteria: The code should include a HomeComponent class decorated with @Component, having selector 'app-home' and a template with an <h2> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the HomeComponent with a simple template. This component will serve as the home page for your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the HomeComponent, but make sure it has the @Component decorator with both selector and template properties defined correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HomeComponent wasn't created correctly. Remember to use @Component decorator with selector 'app-home' and a template containing an <h2> element.

steps.title: Create AboutComponent
steps.instruction: Create a new Angular component named AboutComponent with a @Component decorator and a simple template that displays 'About Page'.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define the component. Set the selector to 'app-about' and add a template property with the text content.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new AboutComponent class is created with a basic template that will be used for the '/about' route.
successCriteria: The code should include a new class named AboutComponent decorated with @Component, with selector 'app-about' and a template containing 'About Page'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the AboutComponent. This component will be used for the '/about' route in your navigation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your AboutComponent has: 1) The @Component decorator, 2) selector set to 'app-about', 3) a template property with 'About Page' content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AboutComponent wasn't created correctly. Remember to use @Component decorator with selector 'app-about' and a template that displays 'About Page'.

steps.title: Add components to AppModule
steps.instruction: Add the AboutComponent to the declarations array in the AppModule.
steps.hint: The declarations array in @NgModule should include all components used in your application. Add AboutComponent to the existing array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppModule will now properly declare both HomeComponent and AboutComponent, making them available for routing.
successCriteria: AboutComponent should be added to the declarations array in the @NgModule decorator of AppModule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added AboutComponent to the AppModule declarations. This makes the component available for use throughout your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the AboutComponent might not be correctly added to the declarations array. Make sure it's included in the array inside the @NgModule decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AboutComponent needs to be added to the declarations array in AppModule. Check that the component name is spelled correctly and placed within the array brackets.

steps.title: Update route configuration with components
steps.instruction: Update the routes array to include the component properties for HomeComponent and AboutComponent.
steps.hint: Add the component property to each route object, referencing the component class names.
steps.expectedOutcome: The routes array now properly maps each path to its corresponding component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully mapped the routes to their components, completing the navigation setup.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both routes have their component properties correctly assigned.
steps.feedbackWrong: The routes array doesn't seem to have the correct component mappings. Check that each route object includes a component property.
